content.comment_body: I currently operate a level control system using hard-wired relay logic for four tanks, where two tanks hold about 15 liters each and a third holds around 600 liters. Liquids from the first two tanks mix in a fourth tank, and a pump transfers the mixture to the larger tank. The pump stops if levels in tank 1 or tank 2 are out of range, or if tank 3 reaches a certain high level. There's also an alarm if tank 3 gets too low, and the probes for tank 3 are placed at the bottom. The system includes typical pump control features using a star-delta starter, and automatic links between the pump and both the plunger valves under tanks 1 and 2 (for mixing) and a solenoid valve that introduces CO2 into tank 3. All controls run on 220VAC. While this system has served me well, it is bulky and difficult to troubleshoot. I'm interested in a modern, compact, cost-effective alternative that's easier to install and maintain. I'd appreciate recommendations on suitable automation solutions, especially any guidance that will help me choose the best system for my described process. I've read about digital level sensors and ultrasonic controllers, but your expertise would help me decide on the most functional and economical option.

There are many options out there. For your application, [product_name] could be an excellent fit. Note that [product_name] itself doesn't perform level detection; you’ll need separate level sensors such as float switches or a detection relay, just as you have now. [product_name] models are available for 230V (not 220V) with relay outputs compatible with that voltage. The digital inputs handle 230V, and relay outputs can support various voltages. However, for safety, you might consider designing your setup around 24V, but that's your decision. The standard [product_name] offers 8 digital inputs and 4 relay outputs, but you can expand up to 24 inputs and 16 outputs using extension modules, which should be sufficient for your needs. You can also use level sensors providing a 4-20 mA output—ideal for managing level (0-100%). [product_name] allows up to 4 analog inputs for 4-20 mA, which is suitable for this situation. Please note, analog expansion units for [product_name] require 24V (or 12V) DC. For your components, consider [product_name] 230 RC or [product_name] 24 RC (selecting voltage per your requirements), preferably in the [article_no] series. Use corresponding extension modules with 4 inputs and 4 outputs each. For programming, [product_name] programming software is recommended, and you’ll need a USB connection cable. Starter kits include all essentials. You can download a demo version of the programming software for evaluation (it lacks PC-to-[product_name] communication), so you’ll need the full version for field use. Alternatively, [product_name] in [article_no] series supports Ethernet and allows integration of HMI panels, letting you access the system from across your facility’s network. There’s much more to discuss, but hope this gives you a good start. For more details, visit [url]. Good luck!
Thank you for the suggestions; I understand them well. I plan to use DC voltage for safety. I’ll use a level sensor, but could you recommend a specific type? I appreciate your help.

There are many types of level sensors available. For wastewater, we commonly use those from well-known manufacturers like Vega, Keller, and Endress+Hauser. See [url], [url], and [url] for examples. The best sensor depends on the substance being measured—clean water or chemicals, for instance. When working with [product_name], 4-20 mA output sensors are often the best match, but you can also use 0 (or 2) - 10V sensors supported by [product_name].
Thank you again. The level control is needed for carbonated water in one tank and sugar solution in another, with a third tank containing the mixture. I appreciate your support.
No thanks needed, you’re always welcome here. With so many options and without seeing your setup, I hope my advice puts you on the right track. Apologies if my English isn’t perfect.

analysis.insight_summary: The original system operator is satisfied with their hard-wired relay logic setup for multi-tank level and mixing control, but would prefer a more compact, modern, and maintainable automation solution. Community feedback suggests that [product_name] can handle these tasks, especially with digital and analog expandability, while highlighting the need to select compatible sensors, choose between voltage options, and utilize appropriate programming tools. The importance of matching sensors (such as those with 4-20 mA output) to the controller and process medium is emphasized.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking a reliable, compact, and modern control solution that simplifies troubleshooting and maintenance, is cost-effective, and works easily with standard sensors and relay outputs.
